name: Lantern-Tide
description: By day, Lantern-Tide is a modest world of slate-gray swells and scattered basalt islets, its low gravity letting waves roll in slow, towering curls. When dusk falls, the ocean ignites: trillions of luminous phytoplankton bloom in drifting ribbons of blue and violet light that trace every current like veins beneath skin. The shallow rift valleys glow brightest of all, seams of cold fire where the seafloor pulls apart.

The air smells of ozone and crushed kelp, and the only sounds are the hush of wavelets against volcanic glass shores and the creak of crystal caverns breathing with the tide. Nights are never truly dark here; travelers describe walking shorelines lit from below as something close to reverence. During storm season, the bioluminescence churns into spiraling whirlpools of light visible from orbit.

Survey teams established a coastal research outpost three decades ago to study the blooms, and they quickly detected something stranger: a structured pulse rising from the deepest rift, repeating every nineteen hours. It does not match any known biological rhythm, and dredging expeditions have yet to find its source. Some researchers believe the lights themselves are responding to it, brightening in the hours before each pulse.

Pharmaceutical cartels have made Lantern-Tide's rare flora worth fortunes, and several syndicates have quietly filed competing claims. But the signal grows louder each year, and the outpost's scientists have begun refusing to share their data. Whoever solves the mystery of the rift will inherit either the greatest discovery of the century—or whatever is waiting at the bottom, asking to be found.
